answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task, then slash that stake if the identity is proven to have double-voted or coordinated with a detected cluster. A lagoon of cheap accounts no longer gives an attacker free influence: every extra identity ties up capital, and successful detection burns part of it. The stake is a beacon for accountability, while a pigment-like trace of repeated funding and behavior can help flag linked accounts without treating similarity alone as proof.
